reason: Both fully satisfy the hard requirements, but Response B gives more concrete, actionable abort/rollback conditions (an unverified/failed snapshot as a hard blocker, plus a specific failover-lag rollback that ties directly to the data-loss risk), and its callout rule at the top of IMMEDIATE ACTIONS makes the snapshot-first constraint harder to miss under pressure. Response A is equally thorough but its single abort condition is more generic and less tied to specific failure points in the plan.
